findings.category: H1B Visa Implications of Extended India Stay
key_points: H1B status requires active employment with the petitioning employer in the US - working remotely from India for extended periods (1-3 years) is not compliant with H1B regulations
H1B is tied to a specific Labor Condition Application (LCA) that specifies work location(s) in the US - working outside the US violates LCA terms
Extended absence from US (more than a few months) while on H1B effectively abandons the status
H1B visa stamp in passport (valid till Oct 2028) is different from H1B status - status ends when you stop working for sponsor or work from unauthorized location
Upon returning to US after extended absence, you would need new H1B petition and visa stamping
Time spent working outside US does NOT count toward H1B six-year maximum or toward maintaining continuous residence for green card
Employer is required to withdraw H1B petition if employee is not working from approved US location
action_items: Notify Disney Streaming HR/legal team about relocation plans immediately
Request employer to place you on unpaid leave of absence (if policy allows) rather than terminate employment
Discuss possibility of leave without pay to maintain employment relationship
Understand that H1B status will effectively end when you relocate to India
Plan for new H1B petition/transfer when ready to return to US (subject to cap if changing employers)
Document all employment dates and gaps for future visa applications
If employer agrees to remote work arrangement, understand this is technically non-compliant and carries risks
risks: Working remotely from India on H1B is violation of immigration law - could result in visa revocation and future immigration consequences
USCIS could issue Notice to Appear (NTA) for status violation if discovered
Extended absence abandons H1B status - cannot re-enter US on expired status
Future visa applications could be denied based on previous violations
Employer could face penalties for LCA violations if employee works from non-approved location
H1B clock continues to run even while outside US if petition remains active, wasting valuable H1B time
findings.timeline: Immediate - discuss with employer before departure. H1B status ends when you leave US for India relocation or when employer withdraws petition (whichever is sooner).
findings.estimated_cost: $0 for status abandonment. New H1B petition upon return: $460 base fee + $500 anti-fraud fee + $1,500 premium processing (optional) + attorney fees $2,000-$5,000 = approximately $4,460-$7,460 total

findings.category: H4 EAD Implications for Wife Working in India
key_points: H4 EAD (Employment Authorization Document) is valid only for employment in the United States

H4 status depends on primary H1B holder maintaining valid H1B status - if husband's H1B ends, H4 ends
Extended absence from US while on H4 status suggests abandonment of status
H4 EAD expires independently and must be renewed; cannot be renewed if H4 status is abandoned
Critical policy change: Effective October 30, 2025, automatic H4 EAD extensions eliminated - work authorization ends on expiration date
Working in India requires separate Indian work authorization/visa, unrelated to H4 EAD
H4 EAD allows wife to work for US employer only while physically in the US
action_items: Understand that H4 EAD becomes invalid for its intended purpose once relocating to India
If planning to work in India, research Indian employment visa or work permit requirements separately
Notify current US employer (West District Elementary School) about relocation plans
Do not renew H4 EAD if staying in India long-term as it will be unnecessary
If working remotely for US company from India, consult Indian tax attorney about employment status and work authorization
Explore spousal employment opportunities in India that don't require H4 EAD
Consider that wife's MBA and cooking/baking skills may open opportunities in Indian job market
Obtain new H4 EAD after returning to US (if eligible based on husband's H1B status at that time)
risks: Claiming to work on H4 EAD while physically in India is misrepresentation and immigration fraud
H4 status abandonment means starting immigration process from scratch upon US return
No guarantee of H4 EAD eligibility upon return if H1B circumstances change
Working in India without proper authorization violates Indian immigration law
October 2025 policy change eliminates automatic extensions - any gap in status is critical
If wife works remotely for US employer from India, complex tax and legal implications in both countries
findings.timeline: H4 EAD becomes irrelevant upon departure from US. Indian work authorization (if needed) should be researched 3-6 months before departure.
findings.estimated_cost: H4 EAD renewal unnecessary if in India ($410 saved). Indian work permit/employment visa: varies by visa type, approximately ₹10,000-₹25,000 ($120-$300) if required. New H4 EAD upon US return: $410 filing fee + $1,500 premium processing (optional) = $410-$1,910

key_points: OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) card provides lifetime multiple-entry, multi-purpose visa to India for foreign nationals of Indian origin
7-year-old US-born son is eligible as he was born to Indian citizen parents
OCI is NOT dual citizenship - holder remains foreign national with special privileges
OCI provides visa-free travel and stay in India indefinitely with no registration requirements
OCI card must be carried with valid US passport for travel
For minors under 20: OCI card requires renewal only once after age 20 when new passport issued (policy updated June 2021)
Application filed through VFS Global in USA with jurisdiction based on residence (Connecticut falls under specific consular jurisdiction)
Online application required first through Government of India OCI Services website, then VFS Global registration
Processing involves: VFS verification (2-3 days) → Embassy/Consulate review → Ministry of Home Affairs background check
OCI holders cannot vote, hold constitutional posts, acquire agricultural land in India (can inherit)
action_items: Apply for OCI card immediately - do NOT wait until departure as processing takes 2-4 months
Register online at Government of India OCI Services website first
Upload digital photo, signature, and required documents online
Complete VFS Global registration with Web Reference Number

Gather required documents: son's US birth certificate, US passport (current, valid till Jun 2029), parents' Indian passports, parents' marriage certificate, proof of parents' Indian citizenship at time of child's birth
Prepare application fee payment ($293.90 total for new OCI from USA)
Submit application by mail to VFS Global (walk-in appointments currently unavailable)
Track application using VFS reference number online
Upon approval, receive OCI card and update it once after age 20 when new passport is issued
risks: Processing delays can extend to 4+ months, especially if additional documents requested or prior MHA approval needed
Applications with missing/incorrect documents will be returned - causes 21+ day delay
VFS Global not liable for applications lost in mail transit
False documents or misrepresentation will result in application denial and potential bar from future applications
Complex cases requiring prior MHA approval can take 30-120 business days
Without OCI, child would need regular US citizen visa to India which requires registration for stays exceeding 180 days
findings.timeline: Apply immediately. Standard processing: 2-4 months. Complex cases: 3-6 months. Recommended to apply at least 4 months before travel.
findings.estimated_cost: New OCI Card from USA: Consular fee $275.00 + ICWF fee $3.00 + Service fee $15.90 + Credit card processing 3% (~$9) = Total approximately $303. One-time expense, lifetime validity with one renewal after age 20.

OCI eliminates all visa requirements and registration hassles
OCI provides same benefits as Indian national except voting rights and government employment
Child maintains full US citizenship - OCI does not affect US citizenship status
US passport must remain valid - son's passport expires June 2029, should be renewed before expiration
OCI card must be presented with valid US passport for all India travel
No restrictions on frequency or duration of India stays with OCI

EB1A requires proof of 'extraordinary ability' - sustained national/international acclaim in field
Building EB1A case while in India is feasible through publications, speaking engagements, open source contributions, patents, awards, etc.

Foreign Tax Credit available for taxes paid to India - can offset US tax liability
FBAR (Foreign Bank Account Report) required if aggregate foreign accounts exceed $10,000 at any time during year
FATCA (Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act) reporting required for foreign financial assets above thresholds
US tax filing deadline extended to June 15 automatically for overseas residents, can extend further to October 15
Self-employment tax not reduced by FEIE - full 15.3% applies to self-employment income even if excluded from income tax
State tax obligations continue for Connecticut - may need to establish non-residence
India tax residency: staying 182+ days in fiscal year (April-March) triggers Indian tax residency

Establish Bona Fide Residence in India by maintaining home, local connections for full tax year
Track days outside US carefully to meet 330-day Physical Presence Test if using that method
Open Indian bank accounts and report on FBAR (FinCEN Form 114) if aggregate exceeds $10,000
File Form 8938 (FATCA) if foreign assets exceed thresholds ($200,000 single, $400,000 married on last day of year)

Register with Indian tax authorities and obtain PAN (Permanent Account Number)
File Indian tax returns if staying 182+ days and earning Indian income
Claim Foreign Tax Credit (Form 1116) for Indian taxes paid to offset US tax
Update Connecticut to establish non-residence if planning extended stay (file final resident return)
Set up estimated quarterly tax payments for US taxes to avoid penalties
Consider Social Security Totalization Agreement between US-India to avoid double social security taxation

Not claiming FEIE correctly results in double taxation
Becoming Indian tax resident (182+ days) without proper planning creates dual tax obligations
Connecticut may claim continued tax residency if home not rented/sold and ties maintained
US retirement account (401k) distributions while in India may have different tax treatment
Foreign exchange reporting violations carry severe penalties - up to $100,000 or 50% of account balance
Indian TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) may be withheld at 30% for non-residents without PAN
Dual tax residency can occur in year of relocation - may owe taxes to both countries on same income
findings.timeline: Pre-departure tax planning: 2-3 months before leaving. Annual US filing: by June 15 (automatic extension) or October 15 (with extension request). Indian tax registration: within 1 month of arrival. Indian tax filing: by July 31 following fiscal year end (March 31). FBAR filing: April 15 (automatic extension to October 15).

TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) withheld at 30% for non-PAN holders vs. applicable slab rates for PAN holders

US-India tax treaty prevents double taxation through Foreign Tax Credit mechanism
NRI status changes to Resident Indian after 182 days - affects banking, investments, property rights
As parents are Indian citizens returning, no FRRO registration required
Income from US sources while Indian tax resident is taxable in India (with credit for US taxes paid)
Remote work for US employer while in India creates tax nexus in both countries

Consider new vs old tax regime choice annually

Interest charged at 1% per month on unpaid taxes
Failure to report foreign assets in Indian return can result in penalties
Working remotely for US company from India may trigger permanent establishment issues for employer
Dual tax residency in year of transition without proper planning
Currency exchange rate fluctuations affect tax calculations and credits
Black Money Act penalties for undisclosed foreign assets are severe
findings.timeline: PAN application: apply within 1 month of arrival, receive in 15-30 days. Bank account opening: immediate upon arrival. First tax filing: July 31, 2027 for FY 2026-27 (if arriving in 2026). Ongoing: annual filing by July 31.

findings.category: Most Achievable EB1A Criteria for Lead Software Engineers
key_points: Criterion 4 - Judging the work of others: Most achievable through tech conference program committees, open source project maintainer reviews, peer review for technical publications, hackathon judging, and technical interview panels for major tech companies

Criterion 6 - Scholarly articles: Achievable through IEEE/ACM publications, tech blog posts on major platforms (Medium, Dev.to with high readership), conference papers at recognized venues (ICSE, FSE, ASE), and technical whitepapers

Criterion 5 - Original contributions of major significance: Demonstrable through widely-adopted open source projects (10K+ stars/significant usage), novel algorithms/architectures with industry adoption, patents with commercial implementation, and frameworks/tools used by major companies

Criterion 8 - Leading/critical role in distinguished organizations: Achievable through technical leadership roles (Staff Engineer, Principal roles), open source foundation involvement (Apache, Linux Foundation, CNCF), standards committee participation (W3C, IETF), and advisory roles for tech startups/incubators

Document all activities meticulously from day one with evidence (screenshots, emails, certificates, download statistics)
Seek roles and activities that span multiple criteria (e.g., conference speaking covers criteria 6 and 8)
Build a narrative that connects all activities to demonstrate sustained excellence and national/international recognition

Judging/Review Activities: Join program committees for 2-3 regional tech conferences (India-based initially: FOSS India, PyCon India, ReactConf India), volunteer as technical reviewer for 1-2 journals, participate in Google Summer of Code as mentor
Conference Speaking: Submit proposals to 5-6 conferences, secure 2-3 speaking slots (can be virtual initially), focus on demonstrating thought leadership in specific technical domains

Patent Filing: Identify 2-3 patentable innovations from your current/past work, file provisional patent applications in India (cost: ₹1,600-8,000 per application), work with patent attorney to file PCT applications within 12 months
action_items: Secure remote position with US tech company or Indian subsidiary of US company to maintain high salary documentation
Create comprehensive tracking system for all metrics (article views, GitHub stats, conference attendees, citation counts)
Begin collecting recommendation letters from senior colleagues, managers, and industry experts who can attest to your contributions
Join professional organizations: IEEE Computer Society ($99/year), ACM ($99/year) - helps establish professional standing

Industry Recognition Activities: Apply for technical awards (Google Open Source Peer Bonus, Microsoft MVP, GitHub Stars), speak at 4-6 conferences including 2-3 international venues, conduct workshops/tutorials at major conferences

Leadership in Distinguished Organizations: Seek technical advisory board positions with Indian/global tech startups, join technical committees for open source foundations (Apache Software Foundation, Linux Foundation), participate in standards development (contribute to W3C working groups, IETF)
action_items: Media Coverage: Pitch stories about your projects/innovations to TechCrunch, The New Stack, InfoQ, InfoWorld, IEEE Spectrum

Start documenting evidence for I-140 petition: compile recommendation letters (need 5-8 from independent experts globally), prepare exhibition list of all published work, create portfolio showing impact metrics
Consider speaking at major US conferences (Grace Hopper, AWS re:Invent, Google I/O, Strange Loop) to establish US presence
File non-provisional patent applications, aim for at least 1 patent grant notification by end of Year 2

findings.estimated_cost: ₹3-5 lakhs ($3,600-6,000) including international conference travel ₹2L, patent prosecution ₹80K, professional photography/videography for documentation ₹30K, PR/media outreach services ₹50K, miscellaneous ₹40K

key_points: Consolidate Evidence Portfolio: Compile comprehensive documentation for 3-4 strongest criteria with at least 3-5 pieces of evidence per criterion, organize recommendation letters from experts across 3+ countries who can speak to international recognition

Critical Role Documentation: Document your critical role at Disney Streaming with detailed letters explaining impact on major products/systems, secure internal recognition (e.g., Disney Inventor Award if applicable, engineering excellence awards)

Prepare detailed personal statement explaining your journey, contributions, and sustained excellence (critical component)
Conduct final review of all evidence with attorney, identify and fill any gaps in documentation
File I-140 petition in Month 34-36, consider premium processing ($2,500) for 15-day adjudication
Maintain H1B validity throughout the process - ensure employer supports the petition or file as self-petition

Alternative Remote Opportunities: Target US companies with strong remote-first policies (GitLab, Automattic, Zapier, Toptal, Auth0), Indian R&D centers of US tech giants (Google India, Microsoft India, Amazon India) where you can work on US products

Consulting/Contracting: Establish yourself as independent consultant for US clients (can demonstrate high hourly rates $150-250/hr), provides flexibility for conference travel and open source work, requires forming Indian entity (LLP or Private Limited)

Startup Advisory/Part-time CTO Roles: Combine multiple part-time roles with US startups (YC companies often need remote senior engineers), document stock options/equity grants as part of compensation evidence

High Salary Evidence: Need to demonstrate earning in top 10% for field - minimum $140K-150K for lead/staff engineer level, include total compensation: base salary, bonuses, stock/RSUs, can combine multiple income sources if consulting

Research US companies hiring senior remote engineers from India, prepare for interview process 3-4 months before move

Set up proper invoicing/payment infrastructure if consulting (Wise, Payoneer for international payments)
Document all compensation meticulously: offer letters, pay stubs, W2s, tax returns (need for high salary criterion)

Income in INR may not demonstrate high US salary even if high by Indian standards (need US client/US entity employment)
H1B abandonment if working fully in India - consult immigration attorney before leaving US
Difficulty demonstrating continuous extraordinary ability if there's employment gap during transition

key_points: India Patent Filing: File provisional applications in India first (₹1,600 for small entity), provides 12-month priority date, cheaper than direct US filing, can file PCT application within 12 months for international coverage

findings.category: EB2 to EB1A Upgrade Process & Timing
key_points: Current EB2 Status: I-140 approved with Priority Date May 2021, India-born applicants face 10+ year wait in EB2 category (current processing ~2012-2013 for India EB2), upgrading to EB1A can reduce wait to 1-2 years potentially (EB1 typically current or near-current for India)

Self-Petition Advantage: EB1A allows self-petition (no employer sponsorship required), provides flexibility to change jobs without affecting green card process, critical if leaving Disney to work in India

Timing Strategy: Build evidence for 2.5-3 years before filing I-140, file new I-140 in EB1A category around Month 34-36, can request premium processing for faster adjudication ($2,500, 15-day decision), if approved, automatically moves to EB1A category with original EB2 priority date May 2021 (most favorable interpretation)

Priority Date Retention: When EB1A I-140 approves, can request to retain earlier EB2 priority date (May 2021) through I-485 supplement J, provides fallback if EB1A priority date would be less favorable, in practice, EB1 priority dates are usually more favorable for India-born applicants

Filing While Abroad: Can file I-140 while living in India (self-petition), need valid H1B petition or demonstrate immigrant intent, consular processing for visa interview once priority date is current, plan to return to US when final green card stage approaches
action_items: Consult immigration attorney about maintaining H1B validity while in India (complex issue)
Ensure you can document continuous extraordinary ability throughout India stay
Time I-140 filing to maximize evidence but before H1B expires (October 2028)
Consider filing I-140 from US vs from India (attorney can advise on strategic considerations)
Monitor visa bulletin monthly to understand when priority date might be current for adjustment of status
risks: EB1A has higher bar than EB2 - denial risk if evidence not strong enough
If EB1A I-140 is denied, need to fall back to EB2 queue (may lose time)
Premium processing doesn't guarantee approval, just faster decision
Being outside US during I-140 adjudication may complicate RFEs (Requests for Evidence)
Need to maintain valid H1B or have alternative visa to return to US when priority date is current

key_points: Personal effects and household goods qualify for duty exemption if you've lived abroad for minimum 2 years (Transfer of Residence - ToR)
You qualify for ToR benefits having lived in US since Nov 2015 (10+ years)
Required documents: Passport copies, visa copies, employment proof, detailed inventory list, bill of lading/airway bill
Prohibited items: Firearms, narcotic substances, satellite phones
Restricted items requiring permits: Gold/silver above certain value, electronics in commercial quantities
Customs clearance timeline: 3-7 days at Indian port (Mumbai/Chennai) before delivery to Bengaluru/Kolkata
Clearance happens at port of entry, then goods transported inland to final destination
action_items: Prepare detailed itemized inventory with approximate values for each box
Gather proof of residence abroad: lease agreements, employment letters, passport stamps
Hire customs clearing agent in India (moving company usually provides) - cost ₹10,000-20,000
Obtain ToR declaration form and file with customs authority
Keep electronics to personal use quantities only (1 laptop per person, 1 TV, etc.)
Have all original purchase receipts for high-value electronics
findings.estimated_cost: ₹10,000-20,000 ($120-240) for customs clearing agent; zero duty if ToR approved
findings.timeline: File ToR application 2-4 weeks before arrival; customs clearance takes 3-7 days upon arrival
risks: ToR rejection if cannot prove 2+ years abroad or if items appear commercial
Delays if documentation incomplete - could add 1-2 weeks
Duty charges if ToR denied: 35-45% on electronics, 10-20% on other goods

key_points: Do NOT ship: Large furniture (buy new in India cheaper), large appliances (voltage differences - India uses 220V vs US 110V)
Electronics considerations: US electronics need voltage converters in India; better to sell in US and buy India-spec versions
Do NOT ship: Perishable food items, plants/seeds (prohibited), mattresses (expensive to ship, hygiene concerns)
Clothing: Ship all clothing as it's personal and duty-free under ToR
Books and documents: Ship these as they're light and valuable
Kitchen items: Small appliances not worth shipping due to voltage; ship only sentimental items like special cookware
action_items: Sell large furniture on Facebook Marketplace, Craigslist, or garage sale before departure
Donate appliances (refrigerator, washing machine, dryer, microwave) to Goodwill or Salvation Army
Sell US electronics (TVs, gaming consoles) and buy Indian versions with proper voltage
Ship only: Clothes, books, important documents, sentimental items, small personal effects
Consider keeping house partially furnished for tenants - increases rental appeal and value
findings.estimated_cost: $1,000-2,000 from selling furniture/appliances (revenue, not cost)

key_points: First month accommodation: Serviced apartments or Airbnb in Bengaluru near Sarjapur Road/HSR Layout
Serviced apartment cost: ₹50,000-80,000 ($600-950) per month for 2BHK/3BHK with amenities
Airbnb monthly rental: ₹40,000-70,000 ($480-830) for family-sized accommodation
Hotel option: ₹3,000-5,000 per night = ₹90,000-150,000 per month (most expensive)
OYO/Treebo budget hotels: ₹2,000-3,500 per night for family rooms
Recommended: Book 2-4 weeks initially, gives time to apartment hunt without pressure
Kolkata temporary housing: 20-30% cheaper than Bengaluru for equivalent accommodations
action_items: Book temporary housing 4-6 weeks before arrival to secure availability
Target areas in Bengaluru: Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Bellandur (near schools and sibling)
Target areas in Kolkata: Salt Lake City, New Town, Rajarhat (modern, expat-friendly)
Use platforms: Airbnb, Booking.com, NestAway, OYO Life
Confirm: WiFi included, kitchen access, washing machine, parking space
Negotiate weekly/monthly rates (typically 10-20% discount vs daily rates)
findings.estimated_cost: ₹50,000-80,000 ($600-950) for first month in serviced apartment
findings.timeline: Book 4-6 weeks before arrival; stay 2-4 weeks while searching for permanent apartment

key_points: Bengaluru 3BHK apartment rent: ₹60,000-80,000/month in Sarjapur Road/HSR Layout area
Kolkata 3BHK apartment rent: ₹40,000-60,000/month in Salt Lake/New Town (30% cheaper)
Security deposit: 10 months rent (standard in India) - refundable at lease end
Lease term: 11 months standard (avoids rent control laws); renewable
Broker fees: 1 month rent (₹60,000-80,000) for apartment finding service
Maintenance charges: ₹3,000-8,000/month additional (society/building upkeep)
Apartment features needed: 3BHK (2 kids + 1 master), parking, generator backup, water supply, near schools
action_items: Start apartment search immediately upon arrival using MagicBricks, 99acres, NoBroker, Housing.com
Hire local broker (₹60,000-80,000 one-time fee) for faster, quality listings
View 8-10 apartments before deciding; check water pressure, power backup, society culture
Verify: Proximity to schools (Oakridge/TISB within 30 min), proximity to Narayana Health for father's dialysis
Negotiate: First month rent reduction, maintenance charge inclusion, painting/repairs before move-in
Budget for security deposit: ₹6-8 lakhs ($7,200-9,600) - must have this liquid before arrival
Sign 11-month lease with renewal clause; get rent receipts for tax deduction purposes
findings.estimated_cost: ₹60,000-80,000/month rent + ₹6-8 lakhs deposit + ₹60,000-80,000 broker fee = ₹8-10 lakhs upfront
findings.timeline: Search during first 2-3 weeks; sign lease by week 3-4; move in by end of month 1

key_points: Buy new furniture in India: 70% cheaper than shipping from US, proper voltage for appliances
Essential furniture cost: ₹2-3 lakhs ($2,400-3,600) for full 3BHK furnishing
Furniture rental alternative: ₹15,000-25,000/month from Furlenco, RentoMojo (better for 2-3 year stay)
Appliances needed: Refrigerator (₹25,000-40,000), washing machine (₹20,000-30,000), AC units 2-3 (₹35,000 each)
Shop at: IKEA Bengaluru, Pepperfry, Urban Ladder, Amazon India, local furniture markets
action_items: Compare rental vs buying: If staying exactly 3 years, buying is 20% cheaper; if uncertain duration, rent
If buying: Purchase essentials in first 2 weeks, spread purchases over first month to manage cash flow
If renting: Subscribe to Furlenco/RentoMojo for ₹15,000-25,000/month full home package
Prioritize: Beds and study desks for kids (school prep), then living room, then kitchen
Buy appliances with Indian voltage (220V) and Indian warranty
Keep receipts for resale value if planning to sell before US return
findings.estimated_cost: ₹2-3 lakhs ($2,400-3,600) one-time purchase OR ₹15,000-25,000/month rental
findings.timeline: Purchase/rent in weeks 2-4 after securing apartment; delivery within 1-2 weeks

key_points: Sell furniture, appliances, and large items 4-8 weeks before departure
Keep house partially furnished if renting to tenants - increases rental value by $200-300/month
Best selling platforms: Facebook Marketplace (fastest), Craigslist (local), OfferUp, estate sale companies
Donation tax deduction: Get receipt from Goodwill/Salvation Army for tax write-off (itemize donations)
Typical furniture resale value: 20-40% of original purchase price
Estate sale option: Company handles everything, takes 30-40% commission, good for large quantities
action_items: List items on Facebook Marketplace 6-8 weeks before departure (gives time for buyers)
Price to sell: 30-50% below retail value for quick sale
Decide: Keep basic furniture for tenants (bed, sofa, dining table) vs sell everything
Donate unsold items 1 week before departure to Goodwill (get tax receipt)
Sell car alternative items: Outdoor furniture, lawn equipment, snow blower (won't need in India)
Keep Tesla Model Y in climate-controlled storage as planned
findings.estimated_cost: $1,000-2,000 revenue from sales; $500-1,000 tax deduction value from donations

key_points: Route: Hartford (BDL) → NYC (JFK/EWR) or Boston (BOS) → Direct to Delhi/Mumbai → Domestic to Bengaluru/Kolkata
One-way tickets recommended: Uncertain return date due to immigration process
Economy class: $800-1,200 per person = $3,200-4,800 for family of 4
Premium economy: $1,500-2,000 per person = $6,000-8,000 for family (better for long flight with kids)
Business class: $3,000-5,000 per person = $12,000-20,000 (luxury option if budget allows)
Best airlines US-India: Air India (direct), United, Delta (partnerships), Emirates/Qatar/Etihad (via Middle East)
Book 8-12 weeks in advance for best prices; avoid peak seasons (Dec-Jan, Mar-Apr, Jun-Jul)
action_items: Book flights 8-12 weeks before target departure date (by early June for late August departure)
Consider: Premium economy for comfort on 15-20 hour journey with two children
Choose: Direct flight vs 1-stop - direct is 2-3 hours shorter but may cost $200-300 more per person
Confirm: Kids' meal preferences, seat assignments (get seats together), baggage allowance (check 2 bags per person)
Purchase: Travel insurance for family ($200-300) covering medical emergencies and trip cancellation
Arrival timing: Arrive Bengaluru in morning/afternoon to have full day for settling in (avoid red-eye arrivals)
findings.estimated_cost: $3,200-4,800 economy OR $6,000-8,000 premium economy for family of 4 one-way
findings.timeline: Book 8-12 weeks before departure; depart late August 2026

key_points: Climate-controlled indoor storage required for 3-year period: $150-250/month in Connecticut
Pay off auto loan first: $25,000 remaining (reduces insurance costs and ownership complications)
Insurance: Switch to comprehensive-only (no liability/collision needed while stored) saves $100-150/month
Battery maintenance: Tesla battery drain ~1-3% per month; needs charging every 2-3 months to prevent damage
Prepare for storage: Charge to 50-60%, inflate tires to max PSI, disconnect 12V battery or use trickle charger, disable Sentry Mode
Storage facilities in CT: Luxury Auto Storage, StorQuest, Public Storage with climate control
action_items: Pay off Tesla loan ($25,000) before departure to simplify ownership and reduce insurance costs
Book climate-controlled storage facility 4-6 weeks before departure
Find trusted friend/family for battery check every 2-3 months (compensate $50-75 per visit)
Set up Tesla app access for battery monitor to track remotely from India
Update insurance to comprehensive-only coverage (storage insurance)
Before storage: Full detail, wash, tire pressure check, battery to 50-60%, cover vehicle
Leave key with battery maintenance contact; provide written instructions
findings.estimated_cost: $150-250/month storage ($5,400-9,000 for 3 years) + $300-450/year battery maintenance = $6,300-10,350 total
findings.timeline: Book storage 4-6 weeks before departure; final prep 1 week before flight; first battery check at month 2-3
risks: Battery damage if not maintained - could cost $10,000-15,000 to replace
Tire flat spots if not moved occasionally - have contact start/move car every 3 months
Storage facility issues - verify insurance coverage and security systems

key_points: Shipping: Pack yourself (saves $500-1,000), sell furniture instead of shipping (saves $8,000-15,000)
Housing: Negotiate broker fee (save ₹20,000-30,000), negotiate first month rent discount
Flights: Book 8-12 weeks early (saves $200-400 per person), consider 1-stop vs direct (saves $200-300 per person)
Furniture: Buy used or rent instead of new (saves 30-50%), shop local markets vs branded stores (saves 40%)
India living: Cook at home (saves ₹15,000-20,000/month vs eating out), use public transport/Uber vs owning car (saves ₹15,000-25,000/month)
Storage: Pay storage annually upfront for discount (saves 10-15%)
Total potential savings from smart decisions: $15,000-25,000 over 3 years
action_items: Shipping: Pack boxes yourself, only ship essentials, sell heavy/bulky items
Flights: Use Google Flights price tracking, book in advance, consider layovers
Housing: Negotiate everything (rent, deposit terms, maintenance), get broker to reduce fee
Furniture: Check used furniture markets, Quikr, OLX India for gently-used items at 50-70% off
Food: Cook Indian meals at home (groceries ₹12,000-15,000/month for family vs ₹30,000+ eating out)
Transport: Use Uber/Ola instead of buying second car (saves ₹20,000-30,000/month including loan, insurance, fuel)
Subscriptions: Cancel unused US subscriptions before leaving (saves $50-100/month)
Banking: Use Wise for transfers (0.5-1% fee vs 3-5% bank wire fees, saves $500-1,000/year)
Shopping: Buy clothes, electronics, household items in India (30-60% cheaper than US for same items)
Medical: Use Indian health insurance (₹25,000-40,000/year for family vs $12,000-18,000 in US out-of-pocket)
findings.estimated_cost: $15,000-25,000 saved over 3 years through cost-optimization strategies
